blocks.text: Setting up your HR compliance workspace

Start by creating a master database for your compliance documents. Open Notion on your Mac, press ⌘ N to create a new page, and type /database to select a full-page table. This table will hold your employee handbooks, training logs, and regulatory checklists.

items: Create a property for Status to track drafts, reviews, and finalized versions.
Add a Date property for compliance deadlines or audit dates.
Use the Select property to categorize documents by department or regulation type.

blocks.text: Using templates for consistent HR documentation

Consistency is vital for HR compliance. Every time you create a new policy document, you want the same structure. Use database templates to automate this. Click the arrow next to the blue New button in your database, then select New template. Add your standard headers, placeholders for signatures, and required disclaimers.
Managing sensitive data on your Mac

Keeping employee data safe is your primary responsibility. Use Notion's page-level permissions to restrict access to sensitive files. Click the Share button at the top right of your page, then select the specific people or groups who need access. Ensure you are using a secure connection and that your Mac is running the latest version of macOS.
If you need to quickly find a specific policy, press ⌘ P to open the search bar. Type the name of the document, and Notion will jump to it instantly. This saves you from digging through folders.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for storing sensitive HR data?
faq.answer: Notion offers enterprise-grade security features. Ensure you manage page permissions correctly and follow your company's data handling policies.

faq.question: How do I find my Notion version on Mac?
faq.answer: Click the Notion menu in the top menu bar, then select About Notion to see your current version.
